papers.title_in_file: Photon-pair generation in a heterogeneous silicon photonic chip
papers.version_note: The file is the arXiv v1 preprint (2208.13955v1, 30 Aug 2022). The record id says 2023, so a later published version may exist. The text is internally inconsistent in places: the abstract gives the lowest gH(2)(0) as 0.1085, the body 0.0126, and the conclusion 0.0125. The introduction gives a 6 nm detuning bandwidth, the body 4.2 to 10.2 nm, and the conclusion 10 nm.

figures.shows: (a) Cross-section of the multi-layer platform: a-Si:H waveguide about 450 nm wide and 225 nm thick above a SiNx waveguide about 1 µm wide and 235 nm thick, separated by 650 nm of SiO2, on a 3 µm buried oxide over a Si substrate. (b) Side view: 1.5 mm input SiNx, 2.5 mm a-Si:H, 3.2 mm output SiNx, with an inset of the 300 µm interlayer coupler and mode profiles at three locations. (c) Dark-field microscope image of the SiNx/a-Si:H waveguides and coupling region (100 µm scale bar).
figures.confirmed_by: The multi-layer architecture is shown in Figure 1 (a-c).

figures.shows: (a) Coupler loss per transition (dB, 0 to 1) against wavelength (1500 to 1600 nm): about 0.65 dB at 1500 nm, falling to about 0.25 dB near 1560 to 1590 nm. (b) FWM conversion efficiency (dB, -55 to -40) against a-Si:H propagation length (1 to 6 mm): about -52 dB at 1 mm, about -44.5 dB at 2.5 mm, about -43.5 dB at 3.5 mm, about -43 dB at 4.5 mm and about -39.5 dB at 5.5 mm.
figures.confirmed_by: The insertion losses as a function of wavelength are shown in Figure 2 (a).

figures.shows: (a) Experimental setup: mode-locked laser (50 MHz), variable attenuator, four cascaded DWDM at 1552.5 nm, fiber polarization controller, DUT, two cascaded DWDM at 1552.5 nm and 1545.3 nm, then two DWDM at 1559.7 nm, fiber polarization controllers, SNSPDs and a time tagger. (b) Single-photon count rate (kHz, 0 to about 8000) against on-chip pump power (µW) for Stokes (1545.3 nm) and anti-Stokes (1559.7 nm): measured, fitted and no-Raman curves; all rise super-linearly (quadratically) with pump power, reaching about 4000 to 7000 kHz at the highest power.
figures.confirmed_by: In the waveguide, the SRS generated photons are linearly proportional to the on-chip pump power

figures.shows: (a) CAR (log axis, about 2 to above 1000) against on-chip pump power (0 to 250 µW): decreases from above 1000 at the lowest powers to about 2 at about 225 µW. (b) Coincidence counts (0 to 2500) against time (-100 to 100 ns), with a sharp coincidence peak and a low flat accidental floor; the upper inset shows the peak, the lower inset the accidentals. (c) PGR (MHz, 1 to 7) against pump power (0 to 15 µW): about 2 MHz at about 1 µW rising to about 6.5 MHz at about 14 µW. (d) CAR (0 to 400) against wavelength detuning (4 to 10 nm): about 190 to 290 at the seven points, with error bars.
figures.confirmed_by: Figure 4 (b) plots coincidence measurement at the highest measured CAR.

figures.shows: (a) Experimental setup for heralded single-photon generation: the idler is split by a beam splitter into two SNSPD channels and the signal goes to a third, all read by a time tagger. (b) Normalized gH(2)(0) (0 to 0.35) against on-chip pump power (0 to 60 µW): about 0.015 at about 6 µW, rising to about 0.33 at about 56 µW, with intermediate points of about 0.03, 0.075, 0.108 and 0.215.
figures.confirmed_by: Figure 5 (b) plots the auto-correlation function with zero time delay

figures.shows: State-of-the-art table of chi(3) photon-pair sources (reference, material, on-chip pump power, CAR, PGR, gH(2)). It lists Wang 2014 a-Si:H (18 µW, CAR 399, 65 kHz); this work a-Si:H/Si3N4 (0.9 µW, CAR 1632.6, 1.94 MHz); this work (5.6 µW, 373.3, 3.29 MHz, gH(2) 0.0126); Jiang 2015 c-Si disk (79 µW, 274, 855 kHz); Lu 2016 c-Si disk (12 µW, 2610, 1.2 kHz, 0.003); Ma 2017 c-Si ring (7.4 µW, 12105, 16 kHz, 0.005); Ma 2017 c-Si ring (59 µW, 532, 1.1 MHz, 0.005); Lu 2019 Si3N4 ring (46 µW, 2280, 4.8 kHz); Steiner 2021 AlGaAsOI ring (3.4 µW, 4389, 230 kHz, 0.004).
figures.confirmed_by: Table 1 shows the state of the art of photon pair generation through χ(3) process.

papers.what_it_is: An experimental paper reporting photon-pair and heralded single-photon generation by SFWM in a heterogeneous a-Si:H/SiNx waveguide chip, with a record non-resonant a-Si:H CAR of 1632.6 and a pair generation rate of 1.94 MHz.

assertions.value: The authors report a highest coincidence-to-accidental ratio of 1632.6 (± 260.4) at an average on-chip pump power of about -30.5 dBm.
quotes: The highest CAR is achieved at 1632.6 (± 260.4) with average on-chip pump power of about -30.5 dBm.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-device empirical measurement.
assertions.reader_inference: The table gives 0.9 µW for this operating point, which matches -30.5 dBm.

assertions.value: The authors report a photon pair generation rate of 1.94 MHz corresponding to the highest-CAR operating point, measured and estimated.
quotes: The corresponding photon pair generation rate (PGR) is measured and estimated to be 1.94 MHz.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-device empirical measurement.

assertions.value: The authors estimate the photon pair generation rate as N1N2/N12, where N1, N2 and N12 are the detection rates of signal, idler and two-photon coincidences.
quotes: The PGR is then estimated as N1N2/N12, where N1, N2 and N12 donates the detection rate of signal, idler and two-photon coincidences.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines its own PGR estimator.
assertions.reader_inference: The PGR is an estimate from detected rates; the text does not state whether it is corrected for the detection and filter losses.

assertions.value: The authors report that CAR drops to 1335.3 (± 240.9) when the on-chip pump power is lowered further, and attribute this to background noise contributing more as the Stokes and anti-Stokes count rates approach the dark-count level.
quotes: The CAR then drops to 1335.3 (± 240.9) when further lowering on-chip pump power.
This occurs because the background noise contributes more to the result when the count rates of Stokes and anti-Stokes photons are closer to the dark-count level.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result with an author-stated explanation.

assertions.value: The authors state that the dark count was subtracted from the coincidence and accidental counts before computing CAR.
quotes: The dark count has been subtracted from coincidence and accidental counts to eliminate dark-count noise
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own analysis procedure.
assertions.reader_inference: The reported CAR values are dark-count-corrected, which matters when comparing them with CAR values quoted without correction.

assertions.value: The authors claim a record high CAR of 1632.6 (± 260.4) for non-resonant a-Si:H waveguides, a 4-times improvement over the previous single-layer a-Si:H platform.
quotes: we have experimentally demonstrated photon-pair generation with a record high CAR of 1632.6 (± 260.4) for non-resonant a-Si:H waveguides, which shows 4-times improvement
assertions.certainty_reason: Author's record claim, qualified to non-resonant a-Si:H waveguides.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract says 'record high' without the non-resonant qualifier. The paper's own table lists higher CAR values for other platforms, for example c-Si ring 12105 and AlGaAsOI ring 4389, so the record applies only to the non-resonant a-Si:H class.

assertions.value: The authors report that, compared with the previous pure a-Si:H result, their device has 4 times higher CAR and 30 times higher PGR.
quotes: our device has exhibited 4 times higher CAR and 30 times higher PGR due to much lower
assertions.certainty_reason: Comparison with a previously published value, not a same-conditions measurement.
assertions.reader_inference: The ratios agree with the table: 1632.6/399 is about 4.1 and 1.94 MHz/65 kHz is about 30.

assertions.value: The authors attribute the higher CAR and PGR relative to the pure a-Si:H device to much lower propagation and coupling loss through the waveguide.
quotes: our device has exhibited 4 times higher CAR and 30 times higher PGR due to much lower
propagation/coupling loss through the waveguide.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author's attribution; no controlled comparison is given.

assertions.value: The authors' table lists the earlier a-Si:H result with on-chip pump power 18 µW, CAR 399 and PGR 65 kHz. For this work it lists two entries, the second with pump power 5.6 µW, CAR 373.3, PGR 3.29 MHz and gH(2) 0.0126.
quotes: On-chip pump power 18 µW 0.9 µW 5.6 µW 79 µW 12µW 7.4 µW 59 µW 46 µW 3.4 µW
PGR 65 kHz 1.94 MHz 3.29 MHz 855 kHz 1.2 kHz 16 kHz 1.1 MHz 4.8 kHz 230KHz
assertions.certainty_reason: Values of this work are measured; the others are cited from other work.
assertions.reader_inference: The row-to-column alignment was read from the page image; the text layer gives the columns flat.

assertions.value: The authors report that with on-chip pump power of -20.5 dBm the CAR remains about 200 for wavelength detuning from 4.2 nm to 10.2 nm, using a programmable waveshaper as filter.
quotes: With on-chip pump power at -20.5 dBm, the CAR remains about 200 for the wavelength detuning from 4.2 nm to 10.2 nm.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-device empirical measurement.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract and introduction describe the multi-channel result differently (a 6 nm detuning bandwidth in the introduction, 10 nm in the conclusion); the body gives 4.2 to 10.2 nm.

assertions.value: The authors state that the programmable waveshaper used for the multi-channel measurement introduces an additional 5 dB loss, which increases the required pump power.
quotes: The waveshaper introduces an additional 5 dB loss, which increases the required pump power.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit of the multi-channel measurement.
assertions.reader_inference: The multi-channel CAR of about 200 was therefore taken at a higher pump power than the headline CAR.

assertions.value: The authors report a lowest heralded gH(2)(0) of 0.0126 ± 0.005 at an on-chip power of -22.5 dBm and a signal rate N1 of 18 kHz, rising to 0.1085 ± 0.0014 at -16.3 dBm and N1 of 310 kHz.
quotes: The lowest gH(2)(0) is measured to be 0.0126 ± 0.005 at an on-chip power of -22.5 dBm and N1 of 18 kHz.
It increases to 0.1085 ± 0.0014 at on-chip power of -16.3 dBm and N1 of 310 kHz.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-device empirical measurement.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract calls 0.1085 ± 0.0014 the 'lowest' value, which contradicts the body; the conclusion gives 0.0125, apparently a typo for 0.0126.

assertions.value: The abstract states that the lowest heralded gH(2)(0) is 0.1085 ± 0.0014.
quotes: Lastly, we measure heralded single-photons with a lowest gH(2)(0) of 0.1085 ± 0.0014.
assertions.certainty_reason: Contradicted by the body, which reports a lowest value of 0.0126.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract value is the higher-power point (-16.3 dBm) that the body says the g2 'increases to', so it is not the lowest.

assertions.value: The authors define the heralded auto-correlation as N123N1/(N12N13), where N1 is the signal detection rate, measured with the idler split 50/50 into two detectors. The zero-delay value is normalized to the average gH(2) at other 20 ns delays.
quotes: is then calculated by N123N1/N12N13, where N1 donates signal detection rate.
which is normalized to the averaged gH(2)(τ ) at other 20 ns-delays
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own estimator and normalization.

assertions.value: The authors report a Kerr coefficient of approximately 5 x 10−13 cm2/W from degenerate FWM conversion-efficiency measurements, which they call comparable to the state-of-the-art value of 7.43 x 10−13 cm2/W.
quotes: which is comparable to the state-of-the-art value (7.43 x 10−13 cm2/W)
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical estimate from a small set of devices.
assertions.reader_inference: The extracted value is roughly 30% below the literature value.

assertions.value: The authors report interlayer coupling insertion loss below 1 dB per transition over a 100 nm bandwidth, propagation loss of 0.5 dB/cm in SiNx and 4 dB/cm in a-Si:H, and a total on-off chip loss of 9 dB in the photon-pair setup.
quotes: The on-chip interlayer coupling insertion loss is measured to be less than 1 dB per transition over a 100 nm bandwidth
are 0.5 dB/cm and 4 dB/cm, respectively
The total on-off chip loss is 9 dB.
assertions.certainty_reason: Device-level measurements from one chip family.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in their previous work, a careful vertical coupler design optimized the coupling loss to around 0.5 dB per transition.
quotes: With a careful design of vertical coupler, the coupling loss is optimized around 0.5 dB per transition.
assertions.certainty_reason: Result attributed to the authors' earlier work.

assertions.value: The authors state that the lowest reported a-Si:H linear propagation losses are about an order of magnitude higher than those of Si3N4, so many photon pairs generated in a-Si:H are lost on chip.
quotes: the lowest reported a-Si:H linear propagation losses are about an order of magnitude higher than
the high propagation loss of a-Si:H waveguide resuts in many of the photon pairs being lost on chip before off-chip detection.
assertions.certainty_reason: Motivation attributed to cited work.

assertions.value: The authors cite an a-Si:H Kerr nonlinearity of n2 = 7.43 ± 0.87x10−13 cm2/W as ultra-high compared with other silicon-based platforms.
assertions.certainty_reason: Value attributed to a cited work.

assertions.value: The authors describe the fabrication: 240 nm of SiNx by LPCVD, then 225 nm of a-Si:H by PECVD at 300 °C, deposited directly on top of the SiNx waveguides without damaging them because of the low deposition temperature.
quotes: 240 nm of SiNx is deposited using low-pressure chemical vapor deposition (LPCVD).
225-nm of a-Si:H was then deposited by PECVD.
The a-Si:H layer was deposited using recipe parameters of a temperature of 300 oC
we are able to deposit it directly on top of the SiNx waveguides without damaging them.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own description of their device fabrication.
assertions.reader_inference: Figure 1(a) labels the SiNx thickness as 235 nm, versus 240 nm in the text.

assertions.value: The authors describe the photon-pair setup: a 50 MHz mode-locked laser pumping at 1552.5 nm, a 2.5 mm long a-Si:H waveguide, Stokes collection at 1545.3 nm and anti-Stokes at 1559.7 nm with 200 GHz DWDM filters, and SNSPDs with 50-100 Hz dark counts.
quotes: a 50MHz mode lock laser(Calmar Mendocino)
light is coupled through an interlayer coupler to a 2.5 mm long a-Si:H waveguide where the photon-pair is generated.
The anti-Stokes photon at 1559.7nm is collected by two other DWDMs.
The bandwidth for the DWDM ﬁlters are aligned to be 200 GHz.
The SNSPDs have dark-count rate of 50-100 Hz
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own description of their experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that the SNSPD detection efficiency is 85%.
quotes: ciency of 85%.
assertions.certainty_reason: Part of the authors' stated setup.
assertions.reader_inference: The quote starts after the ligature in 'efficiency', so it is truncated at the front.

assertions.value: The authors report that Stokes and anti-Stokes noise from stimulated Raman scattering scales linearly with on-chip pump power while SFWM photons scale with the square of the pump power, and that SRS noise was separated by fitting the power-dependent single-photon counts.
quotes: In the waveguide, the SRS generated photons are linearly proportional to the on-chip pump power Pin while the SFWM generated photons are proportional to Pi2n.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical characterization from curve fitting on one device.

assertions.value: The authors claim that pair generation in a non-resonant waveguide, without microring enhancement, allows more freedom of wavelength selection and avoids instabilities of resonance shifting.
quotes: without the nonlinearity enhancement by microring.
This allows more freedom of wavelength selection
assertions.certainty_reason: Author's argument, not tested against a resonant device.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that they demonstrated multi-channel photon-pair sources with a CAR of around 200 across a 10-nm bandwidth.
quotes: We also demonstrate multi-channel photon-pair sources with a CAR of around 200
across 10-nm bandwidth.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author's summary of an empirical result.
assertions.reader_inference: The body measured the detuning range 4.2 nm to 10.2 nm.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that the low propagation losses of the SiNx waveguide allow a higher photon detection rate at much lower on-chip pump power.
quotes: low propagation losses of the SiNx waveguide, higher photon detection rate can be observed with much lower on-chip pump power.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author's conclusion; no loss-ablation experiment is reported.
